Objective
This application from City University London sets out the purpose of creating a research database which can also potentially be accessed by other researchers using the Office for National Statistics Virtual Microprocessor Laboratory (ONS VML). The database would be used for analyses relating to inequalities in the outcome of pregnancy and inform maternity service users about the outcome of midwifery, obstetric and neonatal care.  

Processing
Birth registration-NHS Numbers for babies (NN4B) records for 2005 to 2007 that have already been linked to Maternity HES will be used for this project. Section 251 permission, given previously to link data for 2005 to 2007, has now been extended to cover data for subsequent years and data for 2008 to 2012 will requested by updating the previous data request and then linked to Maternity HES. 

City University received Section 251 approval on behalf of the research team to do the data cleaning and analysis in the secure environment of the VML at ONS.   The research team is a collaborative group and includes ONS, and Rod Gibson Associates (Rod Gibson is a sole trader under Rod Gibson Associates). The work he carries out is as part of the research consortium and he will work on the data purely as identified below.  In so doing he is working under the auspices of ONS.    For background, Rod is an expert is HES and is using the in-depth knowledge of HES he has gained in this to work on he data cleaning and analysis aspects of the project and is paid on a consultancy basis for the hours he actually does. 

 All however work under the auspices of ONS when carrying out the work.  The collaborative has enabled ONS to provide the secure facilities that are required when handling the identifiable data.  The members of the research team can access the identifiers at the  data cleaning stage, but only in the secure environment of the VML

This application, in conjunction with a further application for Section 251 approval, is to extend the linkage to records of subsequent hospital care for mothers including postnatal admissions and for babies including neonatal admissions. Linkage algorithms will be developed using a small subset of the data in collaboration with the Data Linkage team in HSCIC. The collaborators are those within the research team, and are named on the funding application and have ONS Approved Researcher status.   Their access to data is described below.  Note that where the collaborators are individuals, they would not have individual DPA registration – they would be covered under ONS.

City University London has previously linked birth registration and NHS Numbers for Babies data to maternity HES for 2005 to 2007 and as part of their annual review for section 251 support, in 2011 City University London asked for an extension to link further years data which was approved by NIGB (PIAG 2-10(g) 2005) National Gestational age Statistics.  This involves HSCIC using identifiers that will be sent by ONS from their births files for linkage to maternity HES records by HSCIC. The linked records with identifiers will then be sent back to ONS by the HSCIC. These records will then be linked back to the ONS births files in the VML (Virtual Microprocessor Laboratory). City University London also requests access to the unlinked maternity HES records to improve the linkage rate, and the CAG letter dated 18/08/2014 confirms S251 support for this.

The key steps in order for handling the data are set out below, together with detail on the nature of data that is flowing at each step.

a. ONS births and deaths data (consisting of identifiers only, not full data records) provided to HSCIC by ONS Identifiable

b. HES Data linked to ONS identifiers by HSCIC

c. HES data linked to ONS identifiers provided by HSCIC back to ONS
Identifiable

d. ONS data restored to files of ONS identifiers linked to HES records
Identifiable

e. Unlinked data also provided by HSCIC back to ONS
Identifiable

f. Data held at ONS, and quality and data cleaning work carried out at ONS by members of team under control of ONS
Identifiable

g. Cleaned file retained on one of ONS' own servers

h. Files of data with NHS Numbers removed put in VML for access by researchers
Pseudo, using cohort id

i. City University access data within VML for the purposes of the project identified
Pseudo, using cohort id

For the second linkage, APC data set will be linked to re-admission records for mothers and babies in HES by the HSCIC, using the identifiers that will be sent by ONS.  City University London have approval from CAG for this reference CAG 9-08(b)/2014. City University London will work with DARS production team to develop the linkage algorithm using a subset of the data that the City University of London would like to link and then link the whole dataset.

Data cleaning will be carried out within ONS prior to the linked database being held in the secure environment of the Virtual Microprocessor Laboratory (VML) at the Office for National Statistics.  Access to this data is controlled. After this stage, identifiers will be removed from the data file which may then be made available in analyses by City University London or (subject to obtaining the necessary permissions) other researchers. All analyses will be undertaken in the VML and data will not be released elsewhere. City University London’s first analyses, which are funded by NIHR will describe and analyse daily, weekly and yearly cyclical variations in births and their outcome and explore the potential implications of the patterns observed for NHS staffing and for service users.

The Data Custodian for the database created at ONS will be Emma Gordon, Head of Life Events Analysis and the Information Guardian will be Roma Chappell, Deputy Director, Crime, Regional Analysis and Data Access at ONS.

Outputs
For City University, the above linked dataset will be cross-tabulated and aggregated data will be plotted to describe daily, weekly and annual cycles in numbers of births and their outcome in terms of birthweight, gestational age, mortality and morbidity recorded at delivery and any subsequent hospital episodes. Preterm and term births will be analysed separately and subdivided according to whether or not the onset of labour and the method of delivery were spontaneous. Births occurring at home and multiple births will be analysed separately and the main statistical modelling will focus on singleton births in hospital. 

Patterns of births will be analysed nationally and, where possible, by hospital, maternity unit or NHS trust. All analysis will be undertaken in a secure environment of the VML and only disclosure controlled outputs will be released by ONS for publication. Papers will be submitted to peer reviewed journals. City University London will submit a further paper summarising findings to Significance, the Royal Statistical Society’s magazine which aims to popularise statistics. 

The results will be presented at midwifery and obstetric conferences and the two-yearly international data linkage conference in Scotland. 

Results (in the form of aggregate analysis with small numbers suppressed) will be provided to National Childbirth Trust (NCT) as well as providing services and materials to prospective and actual parents; it also involves its members in representing the views of service users to the maternity services and also participating in research projects to represent user’s views. As stated in the protocol, Mary Newburn is very experienced bringing this together and the NCT will be organising two meetings of their members and others to do this in relation to their project. Public and Patient Involvement is a requirement for getting research funding but NCT would want to do this anyway as they think this is good practice. No one involved in this aspect of the project will have access to individual patient records. 
 
The Patient and Public involvement component of the project is set out in detail in City University London funding application and project protocol. In addition, City University London’s application to CAG, a poster has been sent to every maternity unit to be put on display to explain the project. This follows on from an earlier poster sent by ONS to explain the linkage of NHS Numbers for Babies to birth registration.

To reach lay audiences, the results will be published in an accessible form on the website of BirthchoiceUK. NCT will disseminate the findings to parent representatives and  ‘patient’ advocates serving on maternity services liaison committees and labour ward forums with the aim of highlighting research findings and service users’ views and priorities to clinical managers and commissioners

Benefits
The establishment of the research database will permit additional research into maternity, which can be used subject to relevant approvals including s251 as needed and DAAG approval.  This research provides an accurate resource by combining both HES and NN4B, giving the potential to enhance maternity HES.

The use of data by City University is for this specific purpose.  Reuse of data for other purposes is not recommended for approval.  As identified above, City University do not hold or access the unlinked data.   Any access to linked data is via the VML at ONS, and is subject to controls in place at the VML.
